subject: general
question: Methane, on burning with oxygen, gives which of the following products?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Methane** (CH₄) is a simple hydrocarbon and the main component of natural gas.
 
• When methane burns in the presence of sufficient oxygen, it undergoes **complete combustion**.
 
• The chemical reaction for complete combustion of methane is: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
 
• This reaction produces **carbon dioxide** (CO₂) and **water vapor** (H₂O) as the primary products.
 
• Complete combustion releases a large amount of **energy**, making methane an efficient fuel.
 
• Carbon dioxide and water produced are gases at standard temperature and pressure, with water mostly in vapor form due to the heat of combustion.
 
• In the absence of sufficient oxygen, incomplete combustion may occur, producing carbon monoxide (CO) and soot, but this is not the typical reaction when methane burns properly.
 
• Methane combustion is widely used for heating, cooking, and electricity generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbonic Acid**__

 __
 
• Carbonic acid (H₂CO₃) forms when carbon dioxide dissolves in water.
 
• It is an intermediate in the carbon cycle but is not a direct product of methane combustion.
 
• Carbonic acid plays a key role in ocean acidification but is unrelated to the burning of methane.
 
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide and water**__
 __
 
• Carbon monoxide (CO) is produced during incomplete combustion due to insufficient oxygen.
 
• Incomplete combustion is hazardous because CO is a poisonous gas.
 
• Complete combustion of methane ideally avoids producing CO.
 
 
 
• **Carbon monoxide only**__
 
 
• Carbon monoxide is never the sole product of methane combustion.
 
• It appears only in incomplete combustion scenarios along with other products like soot and water vapor.
